summary: Oscar Pistorius, an 18-year-old double amputee sprinter, is competing at the Paralympic World Cup in Manchester and has been invited to run in a 400m race at the IAAF Grand Prix in Helsinki in July, raising debate over whether disabled athletes should compete against able-bodied athletes.
Paralympic star Oscar Pistorius is set to run against Olympic and world champion Jeremy Wariner over 400 metres at next month's Norwich Union British grand prix in Sheffield.

Oscar Pistorius is scheduled to run the 400 metres against able-bodied athletes, including Jeremy Wariner, at the Norwich Union British Grand Prix in Sheffield, while the IAAF investigates whether his prosthetic legs give him an unfair advantage.

Oscar Pistorius's manager apologizes to the IAAF after the athlete called the governing body "amateurs" and "unprofessional," amid IAAF research into whether his prosthetic legs give him an unfair advantage.
The IAAF is expected to announce that Oscar Pistorius will not be allowed to compete in the Beijing Olympics after he failed to respond to a report on his prosthetic limbs.
Oscar Pistorius was cleared by the Court of Arbitration for Sport to run at the Olympic Games after appealing the IAAF decision that his prosthetic legs gave him an advantage.
Double-amputee sprinter Oscar Pistorius won his appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport, overturning an IAAF ban and allowing him to compete for a spot in the Beijing Olympics.

Oscar Pistorius finished fourth in the able-bodied B race at the Notturna International in Milan in 47.78sec, failing in his first attempt to qualify for the Olympics since being cleared to pursue a place in Beijing.
Oscar Pistorius failed to meet the Olympic A qualifying standard for the 400m and was excluded from South Africa's Olympic team, ending his chance to compete in Beijing.
Oscar Pistorius failed to make South Africa's 400 m relay team for the Beijing 2008 Olympics after Athletics South Africa confirmed four other hopefuls had posted faster times.
Oscar Pistorius sustained head and facial injuries in a boating accident on the Vaal river near Johannesburg.
Oscar Pistorius is set to compete in the 100m and 400m at the Paralympic World Cup in Manchester on 24 May after recovering from injuries sustained in a February boating accident.
Oscar Pistorius was beaten by Jerome Singleton for the gold medal in the T43/44 100m at the world championships.
Oscar Pistorius ran the A-standard qualifying time for the world championships and Olympic Games, winning the 400 metres in Lignano, Italy, in a personal best of 45.07 seconds.
Oscar Pistorius qualified for the semi-finals of the 400m at the World Athletics Championships, finishing third in his heat in 45.39 seconds.
Oscar Pistorius is cleared to compete in the 4x400m relay at the world athletics championships, restricted to the first leg.
Double-amputee Oscar Pistorius is scheduled to run in the 400 m at the World Athletics Championships in Daegu.
Oscar Pistorius finished last in his 400m semi-final at the World Championships, saying he never expected to make the final.
Oscar Pistorius defended his participation in the London 2012 Olympics and the use of his prosthetic legs amid concerns raised by fellow athlete LaShawn Merritt.
Oscar Pistorius failed to qualify for the South African Olympic 400m team after clocking 45.52sec at the African championships in Benin, though he could still make the 4x400m relay team.
Oscar Pistorius defends his right to compete in the London Olympics, criticizing skeptics and scientists who question whether his prosthetic legs give him an advantage.
Oscar Pistorius became the first double amputee to compete in the Olympic Games, finishing second in his 400m heat to qualify for the semi-finals.
Oscar Pistorius reflects on competing as the first amputee in the Olympics and prepares for the upcoming Paralympic sprints, where he says it will be tough.

Oscar Pistorius and South African teammate Arnu Fourie both set world records in their T44 200m heats at the Paralympics, with Pistorius breaking his own T43 world record at 20.30sec and Fourie setting a T44 world record at 22.57sec.
Oscar Pistorius competed in the Paralympic 100 m final, finishing sixth, according to fellow sprinter Ben Rushgrove's account.

Oscar Pistorius lost the T44 200m final at the London Paralympics to Brazil's Alan Fonteles Cardoso Oliveira and angrily claimed Oliveira's running blades were too long and gave him an unfair advantage, calling for an International Paralympic Committee investigation.

Oscar Pistorius questioned the legality of rival Alan Oliveira's prosthetic blades after finishing second in the T44 200m at the Paralympics, prompting the IPC to agree to meet him to discuss his concerns.

Alan Oliveira says he felt "let down" by Oscar Pistorius's claims that he won his 200m T43/44 gold medal unfairly due to taller prosthetic blades, after Pistorius apologised for the timing of his comments.

South African officials filed a formal complaint with the International Paralympic Committee, reigniting the row over whether rivals to Oscar Pistorius are breaking the rules by swapping their prosthetic blades mid-competition.
Oscar Pistorius won gold in the T42/46 4x100m relay final in a world record time of 41.78sec, holding off Brazil's Alan Oliveira, ahead of his T44 100m final against Jonnie Peacock.

Oscar Pistorius returned to competition at the Paralympics and won his 100m heat, as the row over running blades deepened with the South African Paralympic Committee asking the IPC to investigate whether rivals switched blade heights between races.
Oscar Pistorius is set to compete against Alan Oliveira in the T44 100m final at the Paralympics, four days after Oliveira's 200m victory angered Pistorius.
Oscar Pistorius is scheduled to compete in the men's T44 100m final at the London 2012 Paralympic Games.
Oscar Pistorius finished fourth in the T43/44 100m at the London Paralympics, behind winner Jonnie Peacock.
Oscar Pistorius won gold in the T44 400m at the London 2012 Paralympics, setting a new Paralympic record of 46.68 seconds.
Oscar Pistorius is scheduled to race in the T44 400m final at the Paralympics.
Oscar Pistorius shot and killed his girlfriend Reeva Steenkamp.
Oscar Pistorius appeared in court and denied murdering his girlfriend Reeva Steenkamp in the strongest terms.
Oscar Pistorius's family criticizes "sensationalist" media coverage of the murder case against him as he awaits a bail hearing scheduled for Tuesday.
Oscar Pistorius arrives in court for a bail hearing.
Oscar Pistorius appears in court for the second day of his bail hearing.
The detective leading the Oscar Pistorius murder investigation, Hilton Botha, is revealed to be facing seven charges of attempted murder, raising questions about the prosecution's case.
Oscar Pistorius is granted bail by a South African court until his murder trial begins on 4 June, after being charged with the premeditated murder of his girlfriend Reeva Steenkamp.
Oscar Pistorius is expected to make contact with the grieving family of Reeva Steenkamp, the girlfriend he admits shooting dead at his home, according to his uncle.
Oscar Pistorius reported to correctional services in Pretoria as required by his bail conditions after being released on bail for the alleged murder of his girlfriend, Reeva Steenkamp.
Oscar Pistorius was photographed training on the athletics track at Pretoria University by visiting high school students, though his agent later said it was not an official training session.
A South African court relaxed Oscar Pistorius's bail conditions, allowing him to travel internationally and return to competition while awaiting trial for the murder of Reeva Steenkamp.
Oscar Pistorius is awaiting trial for the murder of his former girlfriend Reeva Steenkamp, while Paralympic sport adjusts to his absence.
Oscar Pistorius was fined for unpaid taxes after being forced to declare his assets during his bail hearing.
Oscar Pistorius appeared in a Pretoria court for a 15-minute hearing, where his case was postponed until 19 August and the magistrate warned against "trial by media".

Oscar Pistorius broke his public silence on the first anniversary of Reeva Steenkamp's shooting, describing her death as a "devastating accident" that "consumes me with sorrow," while maintaining he mistook her for a burglar.
Oscar Pistorius's murder trial begins in South Africa for the shooting death of his girlfriend Reeva Steenkamp.

On the second day of Oscar Pistorius's murder trial, neighbours testified that they heard a woman's screams and four consecutive gunshots on the night Reeva Steenkamp was killed, with defence lawyers disputing the witnesses' accounts.

Oscar Pistorius broke down and wept during the second day of his murder trial in Pretoria as a court heard for the first time the sequence of fatal injuries suffered by his girlfriend Reeva Steenkamp when he shot her.

The murder trial of Oscar Pistorius continued for a third day, with the defense challenging neighbors' testimony about screams and a friend testifying that Pistorius accidentally fired a gun in a restaurant and asked him to take the blame.
The fourth day of Oscar Pistorius's murder trial continued, with defence lawyer Barry Roux questioning witnesses Charl Johnson and Johan Stipp about their accounts of the night of the killing.

On the fifth day of Oscar Pistorius's murder trial, witnesses Johan Stipp, Samantha Taylor, and security guard Pieter Baba testified about the night of Reeva Steenkamp's death, with Taylor breaking down in tears twice and court adjourning until Monday.
Oscar Pistorius plans to sell the Pretoria house where he shot dead his girlfriend Reeva Steenkamp to cover increasing legal costs for his murder trial.
Prosecutors closed their murder case against Oscar Pistorius, bringing closer the moment when he must account for his actions in court.
The murder trial of Oscar Pistorius is adjourned until 7 April after a judge's assessor falls ill.
Oscar Pistorius's murder trial is set to resume with pathologist Prof Jan Botha as the first witness for the defence, with Pistorius expected to testify later.

Oscar Pistorius testified in his murder trial that he heard a noise in the night, believed intruders had entered his home, and fired four shots through the bathroom door, breaking down emotionally as he described finding Reeva Steenkamp inside, prompting the court to adjourn early.

Oscar Pistorius faced a fourth day of cross-examination in his murder trial, where prosecutor Gerrie Nel accused him of tailoring his account of the fatal shooting of Reeva Steenkamp, and Pistorius broke down several times while insisting he did not intend to fire at her.

Chief prosecutor Gerrie Nel concluded his cross-examination of Oscar Pistorius, arguing that Pistorius intentionally shot and killed Reeva Steenkamp, while Pistorius maintained he fired believing his life was under threat.
Oscar Pistorius arrives at court for the first day of closing arguments in his trial for murder.
Judge Thokozile Masipa is set to deliver judgment in Oscar Pistorius's murder trial, with potential verdicts including not guilty, premeditated murder, or culpable homicide.
A South African high court judge is due to deliver her verdict on whether Oscar Pistorius is guilty of murdering his girlfriend Reeva Steenkamp.
Oscar Pistorius is convicted of culpable homicide for shooting dead Reeva Steenkamp and is granted extended bail until sentencing on 13 October.
Oscar Pistorius faces sentencing after his conviction for culpable homicide in the shooting death of Reeva Steenkamp.
Prosecution demands Oscar Pistorius be sentenced to 10 years in prison for culpable homicide, as sentencing arguments conclude and the judge sets sentencing for Tuesday.
South African President Jacob Zuma criticizes Oscar Pistorius's defence team for arguing that his disability and wealth should spare him prison, as Pistorius awaits sentencing for culpable homicide.

The International Paralympic Committee confirms Oscar Pistorius will not be allowed to return to competition until 2019 after his five-year prison sentence for shooting his girlfriend Reeva Steenkamp.
Oscar Pistorius was sentenced to five years in jail for culpable homicide in the killing of his girlfriend Reeva Steenkamp and was led away to prison immediately.
Prosecutors announce they will appeal both the conviction and sentence of Oscar Pistorius, raising the prospect that his culpable homicide conviction could be upgraded to murder.

Prosecutors launched a bid to appeal against Oscar Pistorius's murder acquittal and five-year culpable homicide sentence, arguing the court erred in applying dolus eventualis, while the defence opposed the appeal; Judge Masipa said she would rule on the request on Tuesday.
A South African judge granted prosecutors the right to appeal against Oscar Pistorius's culpable homicide verdict, potentially allowing his conviction to be upgraded to murder.
Lawyers for Oscar Pistorius are scheduled to return to the South Gauteng high court in Johannesburg to challenge prosecutors' arguments that he should be convicted of murder.
The parole board at Oscar Pistorius's prison approved his placement under correctional supervision with effect from 21 August 2015, a decision condemned by Reeva Steenkamp's parents.
Prosecutors filed an appeal calling for Oscar Pistorius to be convicted of murder in the killing of his girlfriend Reeva Steenkamp, days before his scheduled release from prison.

South Africa's justice minister halts Oscar Pistorius's release from prison, referring the parole decision back to the review board because he was approved for house arrest before serving the required one-sixth of his sentence.
Oscar Pistorius's parole review is set for 18 September, meaning he will remain in prison until at least mid-September.
A parole hearing to decide whether Oscar Pistorius should be released early from his five-year sentence for killing Reeva Steenkamp was postponed until 21 October.

South Africa's department of correctional services announces that Oscar Pistorius will be released from prison into house arrest the following Tuesday, 12 months after being sentenced to five years for killing his girlfriend Reeva Steenkamp.
Oscar Pistorius is to be released from prison into house arrest after serving 11 months of a five-year sentence for killing his partner Reeva Steenkamp.
Oscar Pistorius was released from prison and placed under house arrest at his uncle's house to serve the remainder of his five-year sentence for culpable homicide.

South Africa's Supreme Court of Appeal heard state prosecutors' arguments that Judge Thokozile Masipa erred in finding Oscar Pistorius not guilty of murdering Reeva Steenkamp, and reserved its judgment.

South Africa's Supreme Court of Appeal found Oscar Pistorius guilty of murdering his girlfriend Reeva Steenkamp, overturning his previous culpable homicide conviction and ordering the original trial judge to impose a harsher sentence.
Oscar Pistorius was granted bail and will take his murder conviction appeal to the constitutional court.
South Africa's constitutional court rejected Oscar Pistorius's application for leave to appeal against his murder conviction for killing Reeva Steenkamp.
Oscar Pistorius will be sentenced in June for the murder of Reeva Steenkamp, a South African court confirms, and he will remain on bail until the fresh sentencing hearing from 13-17 June.
Oscar Pistorius is scheduled to begin a sentencing hearing at the high court in Pretoria for the murder of his girlfriend Reeva Steenkamp.
Barry Steenkamp testified at Oscar Pistorius's sentencing hearing that although he had forgiven Pistorius for killing his daughter Reeva, Pistorius should pay for what he has done.
Oscar Pistorius was sentenced to six years in prison for the 2013 murder of Reeva Steenkamp.
South African prosecutors apply to appeal against Oscar Pistorius's six-year murder sentence for killing Reeva Steenkamp, calling it "shockingly lenient."
Oscar Pistorius arrives for day three of his murder trial.
Jonnie Peacock broke Oscar Pistorius's T44 100m record with a time of 10.85 seconds at the end of June.
Oscar Pistorius's family and Reeva Steenkamp's family respond to his bail release.
Oscar Pistorius granted bail ahead of murder trial.
Oscar Pistorius faces the final day of cross-examination at his murder trial.
